To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inverse temperature β _{c} (N) of three-dimensional lattice gauge theory models with gauge group Z(N) (N even) is unbounded for N → ∞, (2) the three-dimensional SU(∞) lattice gauge model confines static quark charges, (3) the three-dimensional U(1) lattice gauge model does not confine static charges.

(i) the Z(N) lattice model is a good description of a confining SU(N) gauge theory for large N, (ii) the Z(N → ∞) lattice model is an excellent description of a confinin SU(N → ∞ ) gauge theory, and (iii) the Z(2)-vortex free energy is bounded above by a constant for all Z(N) lattice models.

1) The Z(N) lattice model is in the deconfined phase at large N. 2) In the deconfined Z(N) phase, the Z(N) model has the same critical behavior as the SU(N) model at large N, with the same critical exponents and the same critical temperature βc(N).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large N limit of three-dimensional Z(N), SU(N) and U(N) lattice gauge theories.
the large-N limit of Z(N) lattice models in three dimensions.
the large N limit of three-dimensional Z(N).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three-dimensional Z(N)-lattice gauge model is a good candidate for the large N limit of the four-dimensional model.
the Z(N) model is in a phase with a nontrivial vacuum at large N.
there exists a critical value of N above which the Z(2)-vortex free energy vanishes and that the three-dimensional Z(N)-model confines static quarks for large values of N.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
three-dimensional lattice gauge models are very interesting in the large N limit.
we have proved the existence of an infinite sequence of phase transitions in three-dimensional Z(2) lattice gauge theory.
the three-dimensional Z(N ) lattice gauge models at large N are not asymptotically free.
The main takeaway from our work is that
three-dimensional Z(N), with N even, gauge models do not confine quarks for any N.
the three-dimensional Z(N), N even, model is a good model of the three-dimensional SU(2) model at large β.
the three-dimensional Z(2) lattice gauge theory is not a good model for the strong interactions.
